locator.title: Наливной пол трескается и пылит? В чем может быть ошибка
locator.lead: Разбираем ошибки при заливке наливного пола, которые часто приводят к проблемам

nearest_text_before.text: Проблема: пропуск этапа работы с инструментом после заливки. Последствие — образование бугров, ям и кратеров на поверхности.

image_reading: Close-up of a gray poured-floor surface with many scattered pinholes and small craters.
The shallow depth of field keeps the central and upper-right pores clearest; tiny trapped-air bubbles are the only naturally plausible moving elements.
The surface already reads as defective and uneven rather than freshly smooth.
analysis.article_context: The body image illustrates Error No. 6: skipping spreading and deaeration after pouring, which leaves trapped air and produces pits and craters. The animation should make that defect-forming process legible without introducing tools or repairs absent from the frame.

structured_intent.editorial_meaning: Skipping deaeration allows trapped air to leave pits and craters in a poured floor.
structured_intent.primary_action: Trapped air rises through the wet material and opens small pinhole craters at the surface.
structured_intent.terminal_state: Several newly formed pinholes remain open and clearly visible on the surface.
structured_intent.semantic_invariant: The floor surface remains visibly defective and uneven through the last frame.

models.scene_plan: Five-second fixed macro shot. Subtle swelling begins immediately around a few existing pores; trapped air rises at an even, moderate pace and sequentially opens several nearby pinholes through most of the shot. The final second settles naturally with the newly formed craters remaining visible and the surface still uneven.
models.positive_prompt: Tiny trapped-air bubbles slowly rise beneath the wet floor surface and open into several small pinhole craters from center toward the upper right. Fixed macro camera. By the final frame, the new pits remain clearly open across the defective surface.

models.scene_plan: Five-second fixed shot focused on the sharp central pore field. A gradual chain of small air releases travels outward across the visible surface, each release opening a restrained crater while the same defect process continues for nearly the full duration. Motion tapers near the end, leaving a readable cluster of fresh pinholes.
models.positive_prompt: Trapped air gradually migrates through the wet floor and releases as a spreading sequence of tiny surface craters. Keep the macro camera fixed; end with several fresh pinholes visibly open and the surface uneven.

models.scene_plan: Four-second focused macro moment with a fixed camera. A small number of nearby air pockets lift and break through in a concise, steady progression, using lower amplitude and fewer releases than the five-second versions. The last frames show the resulting open pits clearly, with no reversal or repair.
models.positive_prompt: A few trapped-air pockets rise and gently break through the wet floor as tiny pinhole craters. Fixed macro view; finish with the fresh pits open and clearly visible on the defective surface.
